text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx error rate detected on /v1/generate from us-east-1 customers. Current rate: 12% (threshold 1%). Paging oncall.

sara (oncall): I'm taking this. thanks incident-bot. I'm on-call until 22:00 UTC, can do initial triage and handoff if it persists.

lee: i'm secondary. looks like embeddings and generation both flapping. alert graph: https://observability.example/redwood/alerts/181234 (paste)

alex: quick note — last deploy to runtime-pool-3 happened ~2h ago. no rollout flags. rolling back would be noisy but possible.

sara (oncall): first pass: metrics -> CPU on gpu-pool-3 at 95% for 10m, long tails on tokenization service. Error logs show KV cache lookup failures intermittently. sample logs:
```
ERROR pkg/inference/cache.go:142 failed to get KV cache entry: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
```

maria: that rpc error matches network flapping we've seen when a particular host's NIC driver reboots under heavy ACK load. There's an ongoing maintenance ticket for that host last week.

lee: mitigation steps in progress: 1) cordon gpu-node-3-7 and redirect traffic; 2) enable cache-miss fallback to local prefix cache; 3) increase retry backoff for KV client to reduce thundering herd. I've started 1 and 2.

sara (oncall): commands I ran:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-3-7 && kubectl drain gpu-node-3-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
python ops/scripts/enable_local_prefix_cache.py --cluster us-east-1
```

sara (oncall): monitoring impact now. error rate dropped to ~6% after drain, p95 latency same. still seeing sporadic 500s tied to cache rpc timeout.

alex: FYI I patched a retry in staging last week, can promote small fix to prod if we decide. patch adds exponential backoff and jitter to KV client.

maria: if we promote, expect a short window of connection churn. signal should be reduced, but coordinate with routing team.

lee: coverage note: I'm remote after 21:30 UTC and may have limited connectivity. sara, if you need escalation after 21:45, ping alex who can take over the bridge.

sara (oncall): handoff plan for next shift (copying into thread for incoming):
- Primary: alex (starts 22:00 UTC) — takeover command: `ops take-oncall --shift 22:00 --from sara`
- Secondary: lee
- Ongoing alerts: high 5xx on /v1/generate; nodes cordoned: gpu-node-3-7; temp fallback enabled for KV cache
- Mitigations in progress: node drain complete, local-prefix fallback enabled, retry backoff change staged but not deployed
- Runbook pointers: https://runbooks.redwood/incidents/cache-kv-failures and https://runbooks.redwood/oncall/handoffs
- Customer impact: degraded generation for ~5% of requests, mostly long-context jobs; enterprise customers on dedicated capacity unaffected per initial checks
- Communication: I'll prepare a short status for SRE channel + PagerDuty incident notes in the next 15m

alex: got it. i'll be on the bridge at 22:00 UTC. plan for me: validate retry patch in canary (2 pods) and then roll to remaining pool if green. if rollback needed, we'll re-enable old routing policy to edge-cache.

ops-bot: Reminder: create incident ticket and link accounts affected -> https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-EO1

sara (oncall): leaving a final action item for next shift: if 5xx <1% for 30m AND p95 latency stable, uncordon gpu-node-3-7 and remove local-prefix fallback. otherwise continue rollout of retry patch.

lee: :thumbsup: i'll keep an eye on bot alerts and paging. tagging @eng-runtime in case kernel driver team needs to follow up.

sara (oncall): ok locking this handoff. anyone else add anything before i go offline for 10m to document?
